correctness.rationale: In the Frobenius-equivariant Cayley description an odd theta is an octad pair in the even-subset model based at the distinguished even theta. The four contact divisors are cut out by a conic exactly when their sum is 2K (canonical sections of 2K are restrictions of conics), equivalently the four affine theta differences sum to zero. The parity mask of their four distinct edges is then either zero or all eight vertices, forcing a simple four-cycle or a perfect matching respectively. This gives the stated 210+105 objects. An independent stabilizer-character computation, rather than enumeration of tetrads, used the intersection sizes of symmetric-group conjugacy classes with D_8×S_4 (D_8 of order 8) and C_2 wr S_4. Fixed counts of powers and divisor inversion recover every displayed row, including the combined spectra, rational bitangent counts and complete splitting degrees. Edges incident to a 5- or 7-cycle have orbit length divisible by 5 or 7, leaving too few remaining vertices to support a fixed tetrad. Without such a cycle, pair corresponding vertices on equal-length odd cycles and antipodes on even cycles, or use the explicit invariant four-cycles in the four exceptional unmatched-odd types. The three rational-tetrad/no-rational-bitangent cases and the finite-scheme Euler products follow. This is conditional on the stable regular octad, not a realizability assertion.
residual_risks: No assertion about Frobenius actions not preserving an octad or realization of all 22 types over a fixed finite field.

evidence: For each divisor d of the permutation order, let F(d) be the value of the existing character at sigma^d. Then the number of cycles of length d is (F(d) minus sum of e times their counts for proper divisors e of d) divided by d. The same arithmetic works on the matching fixed-count column; subtracting yields the four-cycle profile. No finite-field realization question enters this computation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The combined table is fully implied by the published character. The component table is also an elementary evaluation of the prior graph model, with the matching fixed counts already available separately. The rational criterion reads the value at sigma, the no-bitangent cases compare that value to binomial(m_1,2)+m_2, and the splitting degree and zeta are elementary functions of the recovered lengths. These are not additional independent invariants.
